newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks ring in Year of Ox with further gain.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks ring in Year of Ox with further gain.

text.p: Taiwan share prices rang in the Year of the Ox with a gain, showing there still may be life in a rally begun before the weeklong Chinese lunar new year holiday shutdown, brokers said.
The index ended up 63.59 points or 0.87 percent at a six year high 7,410.47. That surpassed the 7,347.74 close of June 4, 1990, and was highest since the 7,857.01 close on June 2, 1990.
Tuesday's turnover was a relatively heavy T$78.4 billion.
"Most securities newspapers expected a rise for the first trading day after the holiday, boosting sentiment despite the index's recent gains," said Eric Liu of National Securities.
It was the sixth consecutive rise for the index.
Electronics led the gains on hopes for high dividends, with Asustek up by the daily seven percent limit to T$347 and Inventec was also limit up to T$223.

"Entering the dividend-issue season starting from March, these electronics shares that have high dividend potential will continue to attract bargain hunting," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.
Analysts have predicted Asustek's earnings per share for 1997 would exceed T$30 and Inventec to surpass T$20, the two highest among all listed shares.

After the close, Taiwan Semiconductor, Taiwan's top chipmaker, set the tone for the sector by announcing a 28.6 percent jump in 1996 net profits. Taiwan Semiconductor shares had gained 50 cents to T$58 in Tuesday's session.
Brokers cautioned that high-tech shares had fallen on Wall Street. "Wall Street's fall on electronics may later affect Taiwan's gains on electronics," Liu of National said.

Constructions and asset-backed shares also were strong as an apparent inflation hedge after local newspapers reported that charges for water and, in turn, electricity may surge in 1997, brokers said. Pao Shiang was limit up to T$26.9.
